target_customer: Delivery platforms and merchants doing last-mile delivery
problem: Delivery fees on inexpensive items were high, so cheap autonomous sidewalk robots could cut last-mile cost.
business_model: Robots operated for delivery partners such as Postmates, DoorDash and Instacart (pilots)

founders.name: Rui Li
education: MIT PhD, computer vision and robotics (per company description)
founders.background_notes: Palo Alto Online (2017) says both founders were MIT students; YC page says two MIT PhDs.

founders.name: Dheera Venkatraman
founders.background_notes: PR Newswire 2018 release says he is from MIT with a robotics PhD.

technical_complexity.rationale: Sidewalk autonomy with mapping, perception and remote monitoring is hard; in 2017 each robot still had a human handler.

defensibility.rationale: Several well-funded rivals were building similar robots and partnerships with delivery platforms were non-exclusive.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Starship expanded with Postmates and DoorDash in 2017; Marble partnered with Yelp Eat24 in 2017. No acquisition of Robby found.

market_need_then: Postmates worked with Robby from early 2017 and Instacart and DoorDash were early customers per the 2018 release, showing delivery platforms wanted cheaper last-mile options.

identity.mascot_or_character: The delivery robots themselves, named Robby

branding.brand_signature: Robot named Robby delivering snacks at Nvidia GTC 2018
branding.community_and_virality: Delivered snacks at Nvidia GTC 2018 per the company release; a later unrelated YC company is also called Robby.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly robot name with some trade press, but limited public brand evidence and overshadowed by Starship.

outcome_analysis: Robby ran pilots with Postmates, DoorDash and Instacart and raised a small seed around 2018, but delivery robots needed far more capital and faced better-funded Starship and Marble. The last dated news is from 2018 and no shutdown announcement exists, so the failure factors are inferred and low confidence.
notes: Website robby.io returned 503. Both seed rounds rest on single database pages (Seedtable, which returned 403 on fetch so details come from search snippets). StartupIntros reports 3M for 2018-09 and different investors from CB Insights, whose total is 2.12M, so amounts conflict. The 2016-09 round has no amount found. Competitors Starship, Marble and Dispatch are only documented in 2017 coverage (thespoon, April 2017, 8 months after the batch) and later pages, so the list is left empty rather than extend as_of. Cause of inactivity not public.
